text.p: Mexican glass giant Vitro SA said on Friday that company shareholders voted to suspend the dividend payment corresponding to 1996 in an effort to strengthen the company's balance sheet.
Vitro also said in a statement that shareholders approved the sale of the Materias Primas unit to the U.S. firm Unimin Corporation.

"The dividend suspension and the sale of Materias Primas are two more steps in the strengthening of our balance sheet according to the 18-month plan that we have been following since mid-1996," Federico Sada Gonzalez, chief executive officer of Vitro, said in the statement.
Vitro said on April 17 that it reached an agreement to sell Materias Primas to Unimin for $131 million.
Sada also said that Vitro would continue to "emphasize and strengthen" its core businesses, flat glass and glass containers.
Vitro, based in Monterrey, Mexico, also makes automotive glass, glassware, plastic containers, aluminum cans and household goods.
